automated_integration_testing_justificat: The Validate Skills workflow runs the automated test suites on every pull request and every commit to main: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/.github/workflows/validate-skills.yml>.
build_common_tools_justification: No build step is required for the interpreted source and Markdown artifacts.
build_floss_tools_justification: No build step is required; all validation and development tools are FLOSS.
build_justification: The project distributes Markdown skill instructions and interpreted Python source directly; it has no compiled build artifact.
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Ruff linting runs through pre-commit locally and in the Validate Skills workflow: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/.pre-commit-config.yaml>.
coding_standards_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md identifies Ruff linting as the required Python coding-standard enforcement: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents contribution, validation, testing, review, and security requirements.
crypto_call_justification: The project does not implement or directly call cryptographic functionality; authentication and HTTPS are provided by GitHub tooling.
crypto_floss_justification: The project does not implement or bundle cryptographic software.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project does not manage cryptographic keys or select key lengths.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project does not collect or store passwords.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project does not implement a network protocol or TLS configuration.
crypto_published_justification: The project does not implement cryptographic algorithms.
crypto_random_justification: The project does not generate security-sensitive random values.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The project does not implement cryptographic functionality.
crypto_working_justification: The project does not implement cryptographic functionality.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Source is delivered over HTTPS from GitHub, every state is identified by a Git SHA, GitHub Actions dependencies are pinned by SHA, and the main ruleset requires signed commits.
description_good_justification: README.md describes the project's purpose, scope, included skills, security model, installation, and use.
documentation_basics_justification: Installation and use are documented in README.md; architecture and security design are documented in docs/architecture.md.
documentation_interface_justification: Each skill's SKILL.md documents its agent-facing interface, inputs, workflow, outputs, safety constraints, and failure behavior; Python CLIs provide --help.
documentation_quick_start_justification: README.md provides a Quick start section for installing and using the skills: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/README.md>.
documentation_roadmap_justification: ROADMAP.md documents the project's intended and out-of-scope work for the next 12 months: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/ROADMAP.md>.
documentation_security_justification: SECURITY.md documents security expectations, private reporting, and the GitHub-based response process: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/SECURITY.md>.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Python tests run without optimization, so assertions and unittest checks remain enabled.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: The automated test suite passes with no outstanding failures; failures block the required validation check.
dynamic_analysis_justification: Automated Python unit tests execute security-sensitive transformation behavior for every pull request and commit to main.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project contains no C, C++, or other native memory-unsafe compiled code requiring memory-safety dynamic analysis.
english_justification: Project documentation is maintained in English.
enhancement_responses_justification: There have been no eligible non-maintainer enhancement requests in the assessment period; future requests are monitored through GitHub Issues.
governance_justification: GOVERNANCE.md documents a transparent, CNCF-inspired single-maintainer decision-making model: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/GOVERNANCE.md>.
interact_justification: Users can interact through the public GitHub issue tracker and pull requests.
know_common_errors_justification: The project explicitly addresses credential disclosure, command injection, path traversal, untrusted repository content, unsafe workflow permissions, and supply-chain dependency risks.
know_secure_design_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and docs/architecture.md document secure-design expectations, trust boundaries, least privilege, credential handling, review, and validation.
maintained_justification: The project is actively maintained on its default branch with automated dependency updates and public issue tracking.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: Secret scanning and push protection are enabled; no open secret-scanning alerts exist, and project policy prohibits persisting or logging credentials.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md records user-visible changes for the continuously delivered project: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md>.
release_notes_vulns_justification: CHANGELOG.md has a Security section and requires security fixes to identify affected behavior and recommended user action.
repo_interim_justification: Git branches and pull requests publicly retain reviewable interim versions before merge.
report_archive_justification: GitHub Issues provide a public, searchable archive of defect and enhancement reports.
report_responses_justification: There have been no eligible non-maintainer bug reports in the assessment period; future reports are monitored through GitHub Issues.
report_tracker_justification: Public non-sensitive defects are tracked in GitHub Issues with a structured bug-report template.
roles_responsibilities_justification: GOVERNANCE.md identifies the sole maintainer and contributor responsibilities: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/GOVERNANCE.md>.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL checks for common vulnerability classes in Python and GitHub Actions.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: CodeQL and Ruff report no unresolved findings in the assessed revision; future findings are tracked in GitHub code scanning and required CI.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL analyzes Python and GitHub Actions on every pull request, every commit to main, and weekly.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on pull requests, every commit to main, and a weekly schedule.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The Validate Skills workflow runs compilation, lint, and unit tests on every pull request and every commit to main.
test_invocation_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents a single unittest discovery command for running the automated suite.
test_justification: The repository contains an automated unittest suite for security-sensitive workflow permission transformations.
test_most_justification: Automated tests cover the most security-sensitive transformation logic, but do not yet cover most analysis orchestration paths.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires automated tests for behavior changes or a pull-request explanation when automation is impractical.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires automated tests for major new functionality: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/CONTRIBUTING.md>.
tests_are_added_justification: The contribution policy requires regression tests for new functionality and bug fixes where practical.
tests_documented_added_justification: The testing requirement and commands are documented in CONTRIBUTING.md.
version_semver_justification: v1.2.0 is published as a v{major}.{minor}.{patch} SemVer release tag via the automated release workflow: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/releases/tag/v1.2.0>.
version_tags_justification: v1.2.0 and prior release tags (v1.1.3, v1.1.4, v1.1.5, v1.1.6) are published as SemVer version tags via the automated release workflow: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/releases>.
version_unique_justification: The project is continuously delivered from Git. Each delivered state is identified by its Git commit SHA, and the protected main branch rejects non-fast-forward updates.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: The project has no known unpatched critical vulnerabilities.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Dependabot reports no open vulnerability alerts and the project has no known unpatched medium-or-higher vulnerabilities.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled and linked directly from SECURITY.md.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents scope, reporting information, response expectations, disclosure coordination, and secret handling.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: There have been no vulnerability reports to respond to; SECURITY.md documents acknowledgement, triage, remediation, and coordinated disclosure expectations.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents GitHub private-advisory triage, remediation, coordinated disclosure, and reporter-credit steps: <https://github.com/RichardSlater/skills/blob/feat/openssf-bp/SECURITY.md>.
warnings_fixed_justification: The CI workflow fails on Ruff, compilation, or test errors; the repository passes these checks.
warnings_justification: Python is compiled with compileall and linted with Ruff in CI.
warnings_strict_justification: Ruff check and compileall run as required CI steps without suppressing failures.
